scope_note: Locations, sizes, licences and formats verified on primary pages via WebFetch/WebSearch only; nothing was downloaded. Rows already typed in AU2_benchmarks.json are referenced, not re-typed. 'not read' means the page was not reachable or did not state the fact; unknown sizes are left unknown, not estimated.

ab02_conditions.c1: exact scored data files released together with ground-truth graphs
ab02_conditions.c2: published per-method scores (F1, SHD, ...) that can be reproduced
ab02_conditions.c3: PC, GES or FCI among the scored methods

ab02_candidates.name: Bayesys repository + Constantinou et al. 2021 noisy-data validation study
ab02_candidates.data_url: http://www.constantinou.info/DOWNLOADS/Bayesys/ (DATA/<NET>_DATA.csv, DATA/<NET>_DATA_<variant>.ZIP, graphs/DAGtrue_<NET>.csv); mirror: https://zenodo.org/record/7682867 ('Bayesys datasets', contents not read: HTTP 429)
ab02_candidates.format: CSV data (discrete, 100k rows per network; the study used the first 0.1k/1k/10k/100k/1000k rows); ground truth as DAGtrue_<NET>.csv edge lists; MAGtrue files for latent-variable variants; raw scores as XLSX
ab02_candidates.size: not stated on any page read (6 networks, 8-109 variables; 100k-row CSVs plus noise-variant ZIPs)
ab02_candidates.column_order_note: Not stated in the repository report. Kitson & Constantinou (arXiv 2206.08952, read) say the default order of their generated datasets is alphabetical, and measure worst-to-optimal (reverse-topological to topological) order effects of +0.036 F1 for PC-Stable and +0.412 for HC. The order of the released Bayesys CSV headers must be checked after download.
ab02_candidates.published_scores_locator: Appendix tables D1-D5 of arXiv 2005.09020 (F1, SHD, BSF, precision, recall, per algorithm x network x noise x sample size); raw scores at http://constantinou.info/downloads/bayesys/results/results_noisyPaper.xlsx
ab02_candidates.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (repository report); data licence on the Zenodo mirror not read
ab02_candidates.reproducibility: The published scores come from Tetrad via r-causal 1.1.1 (PC-Stable, FGES, FCI, GFCI, RFCI-BSC) and bnlearn 4.5. A causal-learn re-run will not match exactly; aim for the same rank order and within-tolerance F1. Networks: Asia, Alarm, Pathfinder, Sports, ForMed, Property. The study gives F1/SHD/BSF per cell, so a released-vs-shuffled order delta can be compared against the published value for the same cell.
ab02_candidates.reachability: constantinou.info is not on the sandbox allowlist (GitHub/PyPI/HF/Zenodo only); use the Zenodo mirror, or ask the user to fetch the XLSX and CSVs by hand.
ab02_candidates.why: Meets all three conditions: fixed released CSVs, ground-truth DAGs, per-cell scores for PC-Stable, FGES and FCI. It also has a published order-sensitivity companion (Kitson & Constantinou) on the same networks. Risks: names are meaningful (Asia/Alarm are memorised by LLMs, so it is unsuitable for LLM arms), the Zenodo mirror's contents are unread, and the primary host is outside the allowlist.
ab02_candidates.label: read (primary): arXiv 2005.09020 PDF, bayesys_repository.pdf, arXiv 2206.08952 PDF; Zenodo mirror not read

ab02_candidates.name: gCastle PCIC 2021 real alarm datasets (gcastle-hub/dataset)
ab02_candidates.data_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcastle-hub/dataset/master/alarm/18V_55N_Wireless.tar.gz ; .../24V_439N_Microwave.tar.gz ; .../25V_474N_Microwave.tar.gz (loader: castle.datasets V18_N55_Wireless / V24_N439_Microwave / V25_N474_Microwave, md5 36ee135b86c8dbe09668d9284c23575b / b4c8b32d34c04a86aa93c7259f7d086c / 51f43ed622d4b44ef6daf8fabf81e162)
ab02_candidates.format: tar.gz containing Alarm.csv (event sequence, read with pd.read_csv), DAG.npy (true graph); Topology.npy (device topology) for the two Microwave sets only
ab02_candidates.size: not stated (tarball sizes not visible; GitHub tree page blocked by robots.txt)
ab02_candidates.column_order_note: Alarm.csv holds event rows, not a variable-by-column matrix. Variable order is the alarm-type index used in DAG.npy (anonymised integer IDs, 18/24/25 types). It is unknown whether that index correlates with causal order, so check DAG.npy for triangularity after download. To run PC/GES the events must first be binned into a count table, and the README does not say how this was done.
ab02_candidates.published_scores_locator: gcastle-hub/dataset README, table 'F1-scores on real-world alarm datasets': PC 0.4299/0.2270/0.1923, GES 0.3393/0.3054/0.2008, PCMCI 0.4226/0.3268/0.2919, THP 0.5765/0.3719/0.3387 (18V/24V/25V)
ab02_candidates.reproducibility: The files are fixed and md5-pinned, and GitHub is reachable from the sandbox. The open question is the event-to-table transform behind the PC/GES numbers, which is not documented; reproduction needs gcastle's own preprocessing or a sweep over bin widths. Ground truth comes from human annotation plus maintenance records (gCastle paper). The device Topology.npy also gives a declared-topology analogue that links to AB-12.
ab02_candidates.why: All three conditions are met on paper: fixed files, ground-truth DAG, and a numeric PC/GES table. Reproducing the PC/GES numbers is uncertain because the preprocessing is undocumented, and the data is event sequences rather than i.i.d. tables.
ab02_candidates.label: read (primary): gcastle-hub/dataset README (raw), castle.datasets.builtin_dataset source, gCastle paper (ar5iv)

ab12_candidates.sizes: Zenodo zips: RE1-OB 31.0 MB, RE1-SS 79.1 MB, RE1-TT 279.7 MB, RE2-OB 1.2 GB, RE2-SS 245.6 MB, RE2-TT 2.8 GB, RE3-OB 190.8 MB, RE3-SS 101.5 MB, RE3-TT 241.7 MB; total 5.2 GB zipped, ~38 GB unzipped (README). ab12_candidates.metrics: AC@k (fraction of true root causes in top k, normalised by min(k, #causes)), Avg@k (mean of AC@1..k; Avg@5 headline); Chance@5 and Lift@5 added Sept 2026 (--report-chance)
baselines_with_numbers: WWW'25 Table 6 (RE2-TT only, Avg@5 averaged over 6 faults): BARO 0.80, multi-source BARO 0.81, PDiagnose 0.67, multi-source RCD 0.54, CIRCA 0.46, CausalRCA 0.43, RCD 0.13, multi-source CIRCA 0.13

ASE'24 'How Far Are We?' (arXiv 2408.13729) Table 5, Avg@5 on OB/SS/TT (= RE1-style data, 125 cases each): PC-PageRank OB 0.34/0.15/0.32/0.33/0.38 (cpu/mem/disk/delay/loss), TT 0.07-0.15; BARO OB 0.94/0.99/0.87/0.99/0.60, TT 0.72-0.99; NSigma OB 0.16-0.55; plus FCI-, Granger-, LiNGAM-, fGES-, NTLR-PageRank/RandomWalk, CausalRCA, CausalAI, RUN, MicroCause, CIRCA (graph built by PC because no call graph), RCD, epsilon-Diagnosis, Dummy (21 methods)
ASE'24 also scores the graph-construction step (F1, F1-S, SHD) for PC, FCI, Granger, ICALiNGAM, DirectLiNGAM, GES, fGES, PCMCI, NTLR on synthetic CIRCA/RCD/CausIL datasets with known DAGs
README reproduction targets: BARO on RE2-TT Avg@5 CPU 0.72, MEM 0.99, DISK 1.0, SOCKET 0.83, DELAY 0.63, LOSS 0.64 (expected output; the paper text says 0.64/0.8 for delay/loss)
ab12_candidates.licence: Conflict between sources: README and PyPI say MIT for code and datasets, the HF card says MIT, and Zenodo says CC BY 4.0. Bundled baselines keep their own licences (CIRCA BSD-3, RCD MIT, BARO MIT; CausalRCA and RUN have none).
ab12_candidates.loader: pip install RCAEval[default] (v1.8.0, 2026-09-29; Python 3.12 recommended; [rcd] extra needs Python 3.8): download_re1_dataset()/download_re2_dataset()/download_re3_dataset(), read_metrics/read_logs/read_traces. BARO alone: pip install fse-baro (v0.2.2, 2025-06-10, MIT) with download_online_boutique_dataset() etc. (Zenodo 11046533: fse-ob 151 MB, fse-ss 127 MB, fse-tt 286 MB; 4 fault types).
ab12_candidates.smallest_useful_subset: RE1-OB (31.0 MB, 125 cases, 5 faults x 5 services x 5 reps, 49-59 metrics, about 12 services) has published PC-PageRank and BARO Avg@5 on the same system (ASE'24 Table 5), so learned-graph RCA can be compared against BARO directly. It has no topology file, so the declared graph must come from the Online Boutique architecture. For a trace-derived declared graph, the next step up is RE3-OB (190.8 MB, 30 cases, traces) or RE2-OB (1.2 GB, 90 cases).
